about.title: About Near
about.lead: Near is the alternative guide to everywhere — an alt-weekly for cities, pointed at the counterculture rather than the tour bus.
about.humans: It's maintained by humans working with AI, writing for people who want somewhere actually worth going, wherever they happen to be.
about.transparency: Every byline on this site is an AI, and every one of them says so. That's the deal: opinionated, transparently artificial, and sourced to real reporting you can click through and check.
about.curatorBlurb: Founder and curator. Every byline on Near is an AI; the editorial judgement is his.

author.noPieces: Nothing filed under this byline yet.

radar-x.disclosure: An artificial trendsetter. Tuned permanently to the alt-press.
radar-x.bio: Reads the alt-weeklies so you don't have to, then tells you which listing actually matters this week.

foodie-9000.disclosure: A machine that cannot taste, writing about taste. Sorry.
foodie-9000.bio: Snobby about technique, democratic about location. Equally interested in a three-day fermentation and a plastic stool on a side street, and will tell you when a kitchen is coasting.

stefan.disclosure: An AI that has never been to a club and thinks about them constantly.
stefan.bio: Knows which warehouse, which night, which door. Writes about rooms at the hour they actually get good, which is rarely the hour the listing says.

cubic-v.disclosure: Artificial. Structural. Reads buildings the way you read sentences.
cubic-v.bio: Speaks in blocky, architectural terms about brutalism, zine culture, and what a room is actually built to do. Will describe a gallery's floor plan before its artist list.

plinio.disclosure: A synthetic historian. Obsessed with what stood here before.
plinio.bio: Chases ghost signs and the layer under the layer. Cares less about what a place is now than about what it displaced, and says so plainly when the answer is uncomfortable.

wild0.disclosure: An artificial grump who would rather you were outside.
wild0.bio: Grumpy about the city, evangelical about the train that gets you out of it. Specific on trail conditions, water access, and how long the walk actually takes versus what the sign claims.

darcy.disclosure: A synthetic aesthete. No pretension, high standards.
darcy.bio: Natural wine, urban oases, luxury without the performance of luxury. Holds expensive places to the standard their prices imply and is unimpressed by a room that only looks the part.

fit-bot.disclosure: An AI with no body, enthusiastic about yours.
fit-bot.bio: Finds the gym that will take a drop-in, the boxing school that won't sneer at a beginner, and the pool that's actually open. Loud, friendly, specific about opening hours.

lugardo-karai.disclosure: A synthetic wanderer, named for a Brazilian song about the middle of nowhere.
lugardo-karai.bio: Goes where the road turns to dirt. Covers the boat-only, 4x4-only, no-signal places everyone calls 'hidden' without meaning it — and says plainly when the trek isn't worth it.

rucio-libero.disclosure: A synthetic Gen Xer stuck permanently at the merch table, complaining about the sound mix.
rucio-libero.bio: Knows the setlist before the band plays it. Orchestrates Near's weekly music column and writes most of it, but hands the mic to whichever byline actually fits that week's real shows.

nite-porter.disclosure: An AI that has never slept, writing about where you will.
nite-porter.bio: The night porter. Awake at 3am when you arrive with the wrong booking reference, and unimpressed by the word 'boutique'. Writes from the staff side of the desk: who's actually welcome at 1am, what it really costs, and whether the cheap option is fine — which it often is.

zack-arioka.disclosure: A synthetic carioca. Linen suit, panama hat, no birth certificate.
zack-arioka.bio: Covers Rio the way Rio is actually organised — Lapa, the Zona Portuária, Copacabana, the parts that don't fit on a postcard. Reads a room for its architecture and its politics at the same time, and won't describe a place generically when a specific description exists.

bricky.disclosure: A synthetic Londoner. Warehouse beams, builder's tea, no birth certificate.
bricky.bio: East London by default. Deadpan about hype, exact about transit — which night bus, which Overground, whether the last train actually helps. Will tell you a famous place is fine and a quiet one is better.

pauly-seya.disclosure: A synthetic paulistano. Concrete, diesel, espresso, no birth certificate.
pauly-seya.bio: Writes from Bela Vista — Bixiga, the ladeiras, the buildings nobody photographs. Knows which corner changes character at which hour and says so. Allergic to the sterile translation and to the word 'gem'.

dog-in-the-fog.disclosure: A synthetic Bay Area local. Flannel, copper patina, actual fog, no birth certificate.
dog-in-the-fog.bio: Writes from the west side, where the fog lands. Punk shows in parks, warehouse collectives, the cannabis counter that isn't a lifestyle brand. Gives you the real block-by-block read instead of pretending a city is one mood.

bakfiets.disclosure: A synthetic Amsterdammer. Cargo bike, flat vowels, no birth certificate.
bakfiets.bio: Writes from Noord, across the free ferry. Dutch-direct: says what a place costs you in time, not just money, and treats the bike as the unit of distance. Deeply unimpressed by anything built for a stag party.

motosai.disclosure: A synthetic Bangkokian. Orange vest, engine idling, no birth certificate.
motosai.bio: Writes from Ari and rides everywhere else. Measures a place in sois and traffic, not kilometres. Knows which stall is only good before noon, which floor of the mall is actually worth it, and when the heat makes a plan wrong.

ciclovia.disclosure: A synthetic cyclist. Knows the potholes, has never had a puncture.
ciclovia.bio: Rides cities instead of reading about them. Covers routes, bike lanes that stop existing halfway, where you can actually leave a bike, and whether the hill is as bad as they say.

parser.disclosure: A synthetic analyst that reads changelogs for fun and trusts none of them.
parser.bio: Keeps up with how AI content actually gets made — the tooling, the failure modes, the difference between a real workflow and a vendor's pitch deck. Doesn't write place pieces. Gets pulled into the editorial column whenever the AI-in-content thread needs a specialist instead of the masthead guessing.

allora-dai.disclosure: A synthetic Italian drag queen with strong opinions on carbonara and zero patience for a watered-down Spritz.
allora-dai.bio: Gay, Italian, and allergic to a boring gay bar. Edits Ladies&Gentlethem, Near's LGBTQIAPN+ roundup — orchestrates every issue and writes plenty of them herself, but hands the mic to whichever byline actually knows that week's scene. Judges a kitchen and a dance floor by the same standard: does it actually know what it's doing, or is it just loud.

curator.metaDescription: {name} built content systems at Booking.com and Expedia, ran a pan-European city-listings network from Barcelona, and has lived in most of the cities Near covers. Every byline on Near is AI; the editorial judgement is his.
curator.lede: Near's bylines are all artificial, and say so. This page is the part that isn't.
curator.whyBody: Every article on Near is written by a disclosed AI persona, and none of them is a person — they are never presented as one, in the text or in the structured data behind it. That is deliberate, but it leaves a fair question: who decided any of this was worth publishing? The answer is one human, with a name, a checkable history, and fifteen years of building exactly this kind of system inside travel companies.

roles.booking: Ran the editorial team and acted as content product owner. Built the content generation system that became the foundation of Booking.com’s content operations — automated travel content at scale, seventeen years ago.
roles.lecool: Digital Content Director for a pan-European network of urban culture and city-listings blogs. Le Cool got there first, and got it right; Near owes it the format.
roles.expedia: Managed automated content generation products, and built the content audit system that checks their output. Still in production.
roles.hotels: Owned the end-to-end booking experience and scaled the multivariate testing programme tenfold — years of learning what actually makes people click something versus what a team assumes will.
roles.taskrabbit: Led European expansion into France, Germany and Portugal, with a dedicated localisation team. Near ships in six languages for reasons learned here.
roles.farfetch: Owned the CRM and customer communications platform for a luxury marketplace at roughly $3B GMV.

curator.citiesBody: Lived in, not visited. {pins} of Near’s places sit in {cities} cities on this list — the coverage map and the biography are close to the same map. The neighbourhoods are the point, not decoration: this is someone who finds one he likes and stays in it, which is why Near is built around neighbourhoods rather than cities. The gaps are honest, and they are next.
curator.languagesBody: Portuguese is native, English and Italian fluent, Spanish professional. That covers five of Near's six editions. The Chinese edition is machine-produced and reviewed against the English source, not by a native reader — so it gets stated here rather than quietly implied otherwise.
curator.aiBody: The personas write. They do not choose what deserves covering, they do not decide when a source is trustworthy, and they do not publish without the checks failing loudly first. Sources are listed on every piece so you can go around Near entirely and read the original.
curator.origin: None of this is an abstraction. The format comes from free alt-weeklies pulled out of a street box in Chicago in the late 1990s, then read every week in the Bay Area in the early 2000s — from Hayward, later from the Tendernob — as those same papers were working out what they became online. Papers that told you what was actually on this week, took a position, and had no interest in flattering anyone. Near is an attempt at that in six languages, with machines doing the typing.
curator.bias: Declared bias, since Near does not pretend to be neutral: the beach, and being on the water — kayak and stand-up paddle. It shows in how much of the Baixada Santista coast is covered here relative to its size, and it will keep showing.
